scenes.title: The puzzle
scenes.goal: Light seemed to break its own rules
scenes.narration: Light always travels in straight lines. Or does it? In nineteen nineteen, astronomers photographed a solar eclipse, and the stars close to the sun showed up in the wrong place.

scenes.title: Space can bend
scenes.goal: Mass curves the space around it
scenes.narration: Here is the trick. Space is not an empty stage. A heavy mass curves the space around it, like a bowling ball sinking into a trampoline.

scenes.title: The straightest path
scenes.narration: Light still takes the straightest path it can. But on curved space, that path bends. Nothing pushes the light. The space it travels through is curved.

scenes.title: Too close to escape
scenes.narration: So gravity bends light. Now imagine something so dense that light passing close to it curves inward and can never climb back out.

notes.summary: Mass curves the space around it. Light always follows the straightest possible path, so when space is curved, the light's path curves too. With enough mass packed tightly enough, nearby light curves in and cannot get back out.

keyIdeas.title: Stars in the wrong place
keyIdeas.explanation: During the 1919 eclipse, stars near the sun appeared shifted: their light had bent on the way to us.

keyIdeas.title: Mass curves space
keyIdeas.explanation: A heavy object curves the space around it, like a ball sinking into a trampoline.

keyIdeas.title: Light follows the curve
keyIdeas.explanation: Nothing pushes the light. It takes the straightest path available, and that path is curved.

keyIdeas.title: The point of no return
keyIdeas.explanation: Pack enough mass into a small space and nearby light can no longer climb out.

keyTerms.definition: Space and time treated as one fabric that mass can curve.
Light bending around a massive object, shifting where things appear.
The straightest possible path through curved space.

notes.analogy: Like a marble rolling across a trampoline with a bowling ball in the middle: nobody pushes the marble sideways, the surface itself guides it.

quiz.question: Why did stars near the sun appear in the wrong place in 1919?
options: The sun's light hid their real position
Their light bent through curved space
quiz.explanation: The sun's mass curves space, so starlight passing close to it follows a curved path.

quiz.question: What would happen to the bending if the sun were twice as heavy?
quiz.explanation: More mass curves space more strongly, so light bends more.

quiz.question: What pushes light off its straight course near a star?
options: Nothing: the space it travels through is curved
quiz.explanation: Light follows the straightest path, and in curved space that path is curved.
